source.author: Jason Pratensis, after Valescus
source.basis: text "Valescus admires pulvis Hali, and Jason Pratensis after him"

2.5.1.3-f13.text: ℞ Epithymi semunc. lapidis Lazuli, agarici ana ʒ ii, / Scammonii, ʒ i, Chariophillorum numero 20, pulverisentur / Omnia, & ipsius pulveris scrup. 4 singulis septimanis assumat.

translations.note: This is the recipe for 'pulvis Hali' (Hali's powder), which Burton names just before it. Epithyme is dodder growing on thyme, and agaric is the purging larch fungus. Scammony is a purgative resin. 'Chariophillorum' stands for caryophyllorum, which means cloves. 'Semunc.' means half an ounce. 'Singulis septimanis' means 'each week'. It is printed as lines of verse, but it is a prose prescription.

source.author: Jason Pratensis, after Valescus
source.basis: text "Valescus admires pulvis Hali, and Jason Pratensis after him"

translations.text: Take half an ounce of epithyme, of lapis lazuli and agaric 2 drachms each, / of scammony 1 drachm, cloves to the number of 20; let all be powdered, / and of this powder let him take 4 scruples every week.

translations.note: Chariophillorum is read as caryophyllorum (cloves or clove-pinks); the sense is uncertain. Epithymum is dodder of thyme. 'Numero 20' means twenty in number. 'Assumat' is subjunctive, 'let him take'.
translations.text: Take half an ounce of epithyme, of lapis lazuli and agaric 2 drachms each, of scammony 1 drachm, 20 clove-pinks; let all be powdered, and let him take 4 scruples of this powder every week.
